name: Japonica
lede: Japonica is a dusty rose-mauve from the Maerz and Paul color dictionary of 1930, named with the Latin word for 'of Japan'.

sections.title: A name without a recorded story
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul list Japonica on plate 4, where they date the name to 1926 [1]. The color books we have read say nothing about it as a color. Where "japonica" appears in them, it is a plant species word inside dye lists: *Caesalpinia japonica*, one of the sappan-type dyewoods, and *Sophora japonica*, the source of a yellow [2][3].

The origin of the color name is therefore undocumented here. That the dictionary borrowed it from a flower or shrub called japonica is plausible, but no source we hold says so, and we do not claim it.

sections.title: Japonica in the dye books
sections.body: The sappan group of red dyewoods is a tangle of names, and the Pigment Compendium notes that species names for these plants are often applied wrongly [2]. *Sophora japonica* yields a yellow from the pistils and stamens of its flowers [3]. Neither is a rose-mauve, so the dye plants cannot be taken as the origin of this color.

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is Maerz and Paul plate 4, J 2, matched by the ISCC-NBS system to a greyish purplish red [1]. It is quite close to [[mineral-red]] and [[indian-lake]] in the same neighborhood, though lighter, and to [[mulberry]] and [[rosewood]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color matches 16 paintings in the ColorHub archive, about 0.07% of it, as photographed [4]. Eight of them are Indian [4], a small sample but a striking lean toward one country.

origin.named_after: origin undocumented (Latin japonica, 'of Japan', is the plant species epithet in the dye lists)
